title: Aaron Rodgers released by Steelers after going  scorched earth on coach Mike McCarthy | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday launched a series of incendiary accusations toward his Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy after being benched only a few hours earlier.

In an interview on ESPN’s “The Pat McAfee Show” on Wednesday, Rodgers accused McCarthy of sleeping through team meetings, missing team meetings and calling the team by the wrong name during a halftime huddle.

The veteran quarterback, who said he is not going back to the Steelers, also said McCarthy was “unwell” and should consider letting someone else lead the team going forward.

Rodgers wasreleasedby the Steelers after the interview, McCarthy said Wednesday.

McCarthy responded to Rodgers later on Wednesday in a news conference, declining to get into specifics of private conversations but stating he believes he has the firm backing of the team going forward.

McAfee’s show has become a regular spot for Rodgers to air his grievances and when the show teased a special guest after the news of his surprise benching, the NFL world braced itself.

Nobody, however, could have been prepared for what Rodgers – who has said he is retiring after this season – would eventually say.

Rodgers started by describing his last week with the Steelers, a week he said summarized what he’s been dealing with this season.

“Last Wednesday, we were in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down and within 10 minutes began snoring,” Rodgers said

“Woke himself up, was rattling his papers, we all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again and less than five minutes after that he walks out the room like nothing happened.”

Rodgers said the head coach was then absent from an offensive meeting on Thursday before failing to show at a walkthrough on Friday and he then missed a morning meeting on Saturday before the Steelers’ game in Philadelphia.

It was during Sunday’s game against the Eagles where Rodgers said McCarthy lost a lot of the team.

“I think the nail in the coffin for so many of us was at halftime, towards the end of it … there’s some rambling or something and without even a heads up he says, ‘Alright, 1, 2, 3 Packers,’” Rodgers said. “That’s what he broke it down on in the locker room.”

The Steelers went on to lose that game against the Eagles, 19-16, to drop their record to 6-4.

The 42-year-old Rodgers said this has been a situation bubbling under the surface throughout the season and since training camp.

“We’ve had these conversations for months now and it began as a concerned friend about somebody who’s unhealthy,” Rodgers said.

“If you’re sleeping in meetings, you’re unhealthy, if you’re not coming to everything you should be coming to as a play caller.

“How many quarterbacks around the league are dealing with the same type of stuff? I gave you one week, I could go week by week throughout the season on stuff that was going on.”

There has been no public information on McCarthy’s health and it was unclear what issues Rodgers was alluding to in the Steelers coach.

Rodgers alleged that McCarthy is often behind on film, even days before a game.

The quarterback also added that he isn’t the only Steeler with this point of view.

“The entire team – offensively especially, really the entire team but offensively – they think that a change is needed because they see it,” Rodgers said.

Rodgers said that during conversations with McCarthy, the head coach has denied the accusations.

“At some point this stuff is going to get out and people are going to realize what is actually going on, it’s crazy and it shouldn’t be like that,” Rodgers said.

The star quarterback added that he should be held accountable for vouching for the head coach before he was hired.

“Full circle, with the first coach when I was starting, back in his hometown, there’s no way he’s going to sleep through his dream job,” he explained.

The Pittsburgh Steelers host the Denver Broncos on Friday with Mason Rudolph stepping in at quarterback.

McCarthy addressed the accusations in a news conference hours later on Wednesday but remained tight-lipped on many of Rodgers’ allegations.

The Steelers head coach started the news conference by saying he didn’t want to discuss personal conversations and he stuck to his word. He also stated that he had a meeting with the team’s leadership council, which he called a “very honest” one.

“It was a meeting, very direct, very honest. I appreciated the opportunity to talk through numerous things that have been on their mind,” McCarthy said.

McCarthy did confirm, however, that Rodgers had been released by the Steelers as well as appearing to corroborate a couple of the quarterback’s claims.

The longtime NFL head coach confirmed Rodgers gave an ultimatum – though he wouldn’t specify what that ultimatum was. However, it seems to align with Rodgers’ statement that he asked McCarthy to stop calling plays.

McCarthy also admitted to an “embarrassing” moment at halftime of the Eagles game, which would be in line with Rodgers’ statement that he said “1, 2, 3, Packers.”

“You know halftime was very emotional, and there was conversations prior to that embarrassing moment, but I just think, you know, we work a lot of hours, so definitely a difference of opinion from what I was told about the comments,” McCarthy said, defending his work ethic after Rodgers said he skipped meetings and fell asleep on other occasions.

Earlier, Rodgers had said that he found out about the benching from tight end Pat Freiermuth and that no one from the coaching staff or front office reached out.

McCarthy threw cold water on that claim, countering that the team tried to reach out to the quarterback and his agent multiple times to no avail.

“We were going through game plan meetings, but I know there was continuous efforts to reach Aaron, and I know there was communication with his agent,” McCarthy said.

McCarthy also added that he holds no grudge for Rodgers after the 63-year-old was fired from Green Bay in 2018. The two were together with the Packers for 13 seasons.
